note: Two execution views exist. The sandboxed view has the Command Line Tools active and cannot see signing identities or mount disk images. The unrestricted view has full Xcode active. Repository-wide swift build/test runs use the sandboxed view; release-style packaging, signing, hdiutil and GUI steps use the unrestricted view with DEVELOPER_DIR set explicitly.
python: 3.14.6 (new scripts stay Python 3.9-compatible, standard library only)
decisions: The owner's Developer ID and Apple Development identities are never used for test or rehearsal builds. Release-style verification uses a throwaway self-signed identity in a temporary keychain, as the plan specifies.
build-app.sh auto-detects identities when --sign is omitted, so every local invocation passes --sign explicitly.
build-and-run.sh runs pkill -x Utter and is not run on this machine, because the owner's installed app is running.
